Your own keywords live in `*** Keywords ***`. A user keyword declares what it
accepts with `[Arguments]` and what it does below. Arguments come in kinds:

- **Mandatory** — `${name}`.
- **Optional** — `${name}=world`, with a default used when the caller omits it.
- **Varargs** — `@{items}` collects any number of trailing values.

Give every keyword a `[Documentation]` line. That text is what editors,
`log.html`, and `libdoc` show — it is how a teammate learns to call your
keyword without reading its body.

## Task 1 — Write a keyword with a mandatory and an optional argument

**Goal:** in `checks/args.robot`, write a `Greeting For` keyword that takes a
name (defaulting to `world`) and returns a greeting, plus tests that call it with
and without the name.

Here is a keyword of the same shape over a different job — repeating a word an
optional number of times. Adapt the arguments and body.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Chants Three Times By Default
    ${line}=    Chant    go
    Should Be Equal    ${line}    go go go

*** Keywords ***
Chant
    [Documentation]    Repeat a word, space-separated; three times by default.
    [Arguments]    ${word}    ${times}=3
    ${line}=    Evaluate    " ".join([$word] * int($times))
    RETURN    ${line}
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `checks/args.robot` defines the user keyword `Greeting For`, and
calling it with a name passes.

<!-- hint -->
Declare `Greeting For` with `[Arguments]    ${name}=world` — the `=world` default
makes the name optional.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Return the greeting with `RETURN    Hello, ${name}!`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Call it two ways: with no argument (uses `world`) and with `Ada`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Greets With A Default
    ${greeting}=    Greeting For
    Should Be Equal    ${greeting}    Hello, world!

Greets A Named Person
    ${greeting}=    Greeting For    Ada
    Should Be Equal    ${greeting}    Hello, Ada!

*** Keywords ***
Greeting For
    [Documentation]    Build a greeting; name defaults to world.
    [Arguments]    ${name}=world
    RETURN    Hello, ${name}!
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Call it both ways and pass

Run it:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

Both tests pass: one uses the default, one passes a name.

**Check:** the test `Greets A Named Person` passes.
